title: Captopril tablets, USP: prescribing information
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling, published in DailyMed (National Library of Medicine); structured product label version 29, effective 27 December 2024, label text Rev. 08/24
funder: not stated. The document is prescribing information approved by the US Food and Drug Administration and published by the labeller, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.
result: Neutropenia below 1000/mm3 with myeloid hypoplasia: one patient of over 8600 hypertensive patients with normal renal function in clinical trials; about 1 per 500 with serum creatinine of 1.6 mg/dl or more without collagen vascular disease; 3.7% with collagen vascular disease (for example systemic lupus erythematosus or scleroderma) and impaired renal function. About half of neutropenic patients developed infections or other features of agranulocytosis; neutropenia was usually detected within three months of starting; neutrophils usually returned to normal about two weeks after discontinuation; about 13% of cases ended fatally, almost all in patients with collagen vascular disease, renal failure, heart failure or immunosuppressant therapy; more than 75% of reported heart-failure cases also received procainamide. Proteinuria above 1 g/day in about 0.7%, mostly with prior renal disease or doses above 150 mg/day; nephrotic syndrome in about one-fifth of these. Cholestatic jaundice progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis and sometimes death has occurred rarely with ACE inhibitors. Angio-oedema in approximately 1 in 1000 patients, with fatal upper-airway obstruction reported; intestinal angio-oedema reported. Cough reported in 0.5 to 2% of captopril-treated patients in clinical trials. Rash in about 4 to 7 of 100, taste loss in 2 to 4 of 100. SAVE: 2231 patients with ejection fraction of 40% or less 3 to 16 days after myocardial infarction, average follow-up 3.5 years; risk reduction 19% for all-cause mortality and 21% for cardiovascular death. Type 1 diabetic nephropathy: 409 patients aged 18 to 49 with proteinuria of 500 mg/day or more, median follow-up 3 years; 51% reduction in risk of doubling of serum creatinine and of end-stage renal disease or death. In 235 normotensive type 1 diabetic patients with microalbuminuria followed up to 2 years, captopril delayed progression to overt nephropathy, but the long-term clinical benefit of reducing progression from microalbuminuria to proteinuria has not been established. Withdrawal of treatment for hyperkalaemia in 4 of 207 type 1 diabetic patients with proteinuria. Abrupt withdrawal has not been associated with a rapid increase in blood pressure.
